jobs.description:
Managing Director – Capital Markets & Investor Relations

Partner Track Premium Properties & Development | Berkeley, California | Hybrid | Full-time

Target First-Year Compensation: $200,000–$300,000+ in salary and performance-based bonus

About the Opportunity Premium Properties & Development is seeking an accomplished capital markets and investor relations leader to help build the next phase of our real estate investment platform.
This is more than a fundraising role. The Managing Director will work directly with company ownership to develop and execute our capital-raising strategy, expand our investor network, strengthen our investor relations infrastructure, and help shape the long-term direction of the business.
Our first major objective is the launch of an inaugural $50 million student housing investment fund
. Our broader vision is to build a diversified real estate investment management company with multiple funds across different property sectors and geographic markets.
This position includes a clear Partner Track for an individual who demonstrates exceptional performance, leadership, cultural alignment, and commitment to the company’s long-term growth.

About Premium Properties & Development Founded in 2002, Premium Properties & Development is a vertically integrated real estate investment and property management firm based in Berkeley, California.
We currently manage approximately 1,000 residential units throughout Berkeley, Oakland, and Albany while continuing to acquire and invest in multifamily real estate across Northern California.
For more than two decades, we have built our reputation on integrity, disciplined investing, strong operations, exceptional service, and long-term relationships. For approximately 15 years, we have also partnered with private investors through individual investment partnerships and real estate syndications.
Our established operating platform, local market knowledge, property-owner relationships, and real estate investment experience provide a strong foundation for building an institutional-quality investment management business.

Key Responsibilities

Capital Raising • Develop and execute the firm’s overall capital-raising strategy.
• Raise equity capital from family offices, high-net-worth individuals, accredited investors, registered investment advisors, wealth managers, institutional investors, and other sophisticated capital sources.
• Build, organize, and manage a strong pipeline of prospective investors.
• Lead investor outreach, presentations, meetings, due diligence sessions, and follow-up discussions.
• Manage fundraising efforts from the initial introduction through final capital commitment.
• Clearly communicate the firm’s investment strategy, operating capabilities, track record, and long-term vision.
• Establish scalable, institutional-quality fundraising processes and best practices.
• Develop a repeatable fundraising model that can support future funds.

Investor Relations • Develop long-term investor relationships based on trust, credibility, transparency, and responsiveness.
• Create a best-in-class investor experience throughout the investment lifecycle.
• Serve as a senior point of contact for current and prospective investors.
• Help establish professional investor communication and reporting standards.
• Maintain consistent communication with investors regarding fund activity, operations, performance, and future opportunities.
• Encourage repeat investment and referrals across future funds.
• Coordinate responses to investor questions and due diligence requests.

Strategic Business Development • Build relationships with family offices, investment advisors, wealth managers, attorneys, accountants, brokers, lenders, and other strategic referral partners.
• Represent the company at investor conferences, networking events, and industry functions.
• Identify strategic partnerships and opportunities that support the company’s long-term growth.
• Strengthen the company’s visibility and credibility within the Bay Area real estate and investment communities.
• Collaborate with the Business Development Manager on opportunities that benefit both the investment and property management businesses.
• Introduce qualified property owners to the company’s property management platform when appropriate.

Strategic Leadership • Work directly with company ownership on long-term growth initiatives.
• Help shape the firm’s capital markets and investor relations strategy.
• Participate in planning future investment funds, property sectors, and geographic expansion.
• Help build the systems, processes, and infrastructure required for an institutional-quality investment management platform.
• Provide insight regarding investor demand, fundraising trends, and capital market conditions.
• Support the recruitment and development of future capital markets and investor relations team members.
• Become a key member of the company’s executive leadership team.

Required Qualifications • At least five years of professional capital-raising experience.
• Demonstrated success raising significant equity capital for private real estate investments, real estate funds, private equity funds, real estate syndications, or alternative investment platforms.
• Established relationships with family offices, high-net-worth investors, institutional investors, wealth managers, registered investment advisors, or other sophisticated capital sources.
• Strong understanding of commercial real estate investing.
• Experience conducting investor presentations, meetings, and due diligence discussions.
• Outstanding relationship-building, networking, communication, and presentation skills.
• Strong professional judgment, integrity, and accountability.
• Entrepreneurial mindset and a genuine desire to help build and scale a growing investment platform.
• Willingness to attend investor conferences, networking events, and industry functions.
• Bachelor’s degree required.

Preferred Qualifications • Experience raising capital for multifamily or student housing investments.
• Existing Bay Area real estate and investment network.
• Experience launching or scaling an investment management platform.
• Experience raising capital for multiple funds or investment strategies.
• Experience working with family offices, institutional investors, registered investment advisors, or wealth management firms.
• MBA, CFA, CAIA, or similar credentials are a plus.

Compensation and Partner Track We recognize that the professional we are seeking is likely already successful in their current role. This opportunity is structured for someone who wants more than another executive fundraising position.
The compensation package includes:
• Target first-year salary and performance-based bonus of $200,000–$300,000+
.
• Significant performance incentives tied to capital raised and strategic objectives.
• Additional incentive compensation for property management relationships that become clients.
• Long-term incentive compensation tied to the continued growth and success of the investment platform.
• A clear Partner Track for an individual who demonstrates exceptional performance, leadership, cultural fit, and alignment with the company’s long-term vision.
The exact compensation structure will be tailored to the successful candidate’s experience, track record, investor relationships, and expected contribution.

Benefits • Medical, dental, and vision insurance

• Paid time off and paid holidays
• Life insurance

• Mileage reimbursement
• Professional development opportunities
• Direct collaboration with company ownership
• Entrepreneurial culture where ideas and contributions have a meaningful impact

Who Will Thrive Here This opportunity is designed for someone who has already achieved success raising investment capital but wants the ability to build something larger.
The ideal candidate wants to create an enduring real estate investment management company, develop lasting relationships with sophisticated investors, influence long-term strategy, and participate meaningfully in the value they help create.
We are not simply hiring an executive. We are looking for a leader who can help build the next generation of our investment platform and ultimately become a key long-term partner in the business.

jobs.description:
Job Purpose

The Office of Hawaiian Affairs (OHA) works to improve the wellbeing of Native Hawaiians through advocacy, research, community engagement, land management and the funding of community programs.

The Administrator functions as the Chief Executive Officer ("CEO") of the Office of Hawaiian Affairs ("OHA") and is responsible for implementing and executing the will of the elected Board of Trustees (BOT). Reporting directly to the BOT, the Administrator & CEO provides executive oversight, strategic & operational leadership, and oversees organizational performance. The Administrator & CEO implements Board policy and advances OHA's constitutional and statutory responsibilities on behalf of Native Hawaiian beneficiaries.

The Administrator & CEO plays a central role in advancing this mission by ensuring that OHA’s people, programs, resources, and partnerships are aligned to achieve measurable results.  The Administrator & CEO maintains stewardship of the strategic planning process, ensuring alignment between Board direction, organizational priorities, operational execution, and performance outcomes.

As the principal executive of the OHA, this role serves as the conduit between the BOT, community, and administrative staff and is responsible for effective communication, leadership and direction.  Additionally, the Administrator & CEO works with other agencies, public and private, that also serve Hawaiians and Native Hawaiians consistent with OHA's mission of bettering the conditions of all Hawaiians.

Essential Responsibilities

Trustee Relations

The Administrator & CEO, selected by the Board of Trustees as the principal executive officer of the Office of Hawaiian Affairs, is responsible for the day-to-day management and administration of OHA under the Strategic Plan, policies, and actions adopted by the Board of Trustees.  In carrying out these duties, the Administrator shall develop, implement, and oversee organizational systems, operational procedures, and administrative processes, and shall make recommendations to the BOT regarding OHA's organizational structure.
Maintains a strong, transparent, and collaborative working relationship with the BOT, ensuring open communication, alignment on strategic priorities, and effective governance support.
Presents complex information to the Board in a clear, objective, and actionable manner, enabling informed governance, and strategic decision-making.   Identifies emerging trends, opportunities, and risks using data and research.

Collaboration/Leadership/Engagement

Responsible for strategic planning and execution.
Establishes clear vision and direction for the OHA staff and ensures that the OHA’s mission, core values, and principles are understood and put into practice.  Effectively mentors and empowers staff to create a healthy, positive, and culturally grounded environment that promotes accountability, transparency, and collaboration.
Fosters a positive work environment with strong values and integrity.  Motivates and encourages high performance and collaboration within all areas of the organization.
Develops and sustains a high-performing organization by identifying, developing, and preparing future leaders at all levels. Establishes succession strategies, leadership development programs, and knowledge transfer practices to ensure organizational continuity, preserve institutional knowledge, and maintain operational excellence.
Assesses the organization’s placement in the employment market to ensure the OHA continues to attract and retain talent of the highest quality to serve the mission.
Works cooperatively and collaboratively with others throughout the organization in alignment with the organization's objectives.

Operational Effectiveness

Monitors all critical organizational functions to ensure high performing operational excellence.
Ensures OHA is consistently aware of potential risks to the agency and its assets and is up to date with mitigation/avoidance strategies.

Fiscal & Asset Responsibility & Compliance

Responsible for fiscal and budget oversight and carries out the management of the OHA’s Native Hawaiian Trust Fund (NHTF) in accordance with the NHTF Investment Policy adopted by the BOT.
Responsible for procedures, guidelines, evaluation, contracts and grants that have been funded to promote services for OHA’s beneficiaries. 
Assumes overall accountability for the OHA’s successful operations, financial health, best practices, and overall legal compliance. 
Ensures OHA’s consistent compliance with local, state, and federal legal and regulatory requirements, , and best practices.

Community Relations & Advocacy

Is an effective liaison between the BOT, OHA, and Native Hawaiian Community.
Builds and maintains strong relationships with key stakeholders and the broader community, serving as one of OHA's three primary spokespersons under the direction of the BOT.
Communicates with beneficiaries and stakeholders in a consistent manner that results in mutual understanding, harmony, and action. 
Manages relationships to create optimal opportunities and moves the organization forward.
Serves as a legislative advocate under the direction of the BOT and is responsible for developing and monitoring the OHA’s legislative package.

Minimum Qualifications

A master's degree from an accredited college or university is required.  Degrees in business administration, public administration, public policy, finance, economics, law, organizational leadership, or a closely related field. An equivalent combination of education and experience may substitute for this degree requirement.
At least ten (10) years’ experience as a senior executive for a non-profit or for-profit organization/company, public administration, and/or executive leadership is required, of which the last five years must be at executive or leadership levels.
Experience leading strategic planning, organizational transformation, financial stewardship, and enterprise-wide change initiatives.
Experience leading similar sized, multidisciplinary organizations through organizational change while maintaining high levels of employee engagement and organizational effectiveness.
Demonstrated ability to develop collaborative partnerships with diverse stakeholders, including governmental agencies, community organizations, Native Hawaiian organizations, educational institutions, nonprofit organizations, and private-sector partners.
Ability to successfully represent OHA before governmental bodies, community organizations, beneficiaries, and the public.
Knowledge of the history, culture, traditions, values, language, and contemporary issues affecting Native Hawaiians.
Demonstrated commitment to equity, inclusion, cultural responsiveness, and community engagement.
Excellent written, verbal, interpersonal, and public communication skills.
Demonstrated proficiency in utilizing technology and digital communication platforms to effectively communicate with diverse audiences, engage stakeholders, support organizational transparency, and enhance operational effectiveness.

Desired Qualifications

Executive leadership experience within Native Hawaiian organizations, tribal organizations, public trust organizations, governmental agencies, higher education institutions, or large nonprofit organizations.
Experience working directly with a governing board of trustees, board of directors, or comparable governing body.
Experience with legislative affairs, public policy development, and governmental relations both at the local, state, and federal levels.
Experience managing complex public budgets, trust assets, grants, investments, or other significant financial resources.

Compensation

The Board of Trustees is committed to recruiting the strongest executive talent available and will establish a competitive compensation package commensurate with the successful candidate's qualifications, experience, demonstrated leadership, and prevailing market conditions.

Pursuant to § 3.10.h of the OHA Executive Policy Manual, the Board of Trustees has the exclusive authority to establish the compensation of the OHA Administrator. In determining an appropriate compensation package, the Board may consider the 2025 State of Hawaiʻi Commission on Salaries Executive Compensation Schedule as one point of reference. The current Tier 1 executive salary range established by the Commission is $225,324 to $263,592 annually.
However, the Board is not limited to any particular salary schedule, benchmark, or compensation range in fulfilling its fiduciary responsibilities.

In establishing an appropriate compensation package, the Board may also consider the successful candidate's qualifications, executive experience, demonstrated leadership accomplishments, current market conditions, recruitment needs, and compensation for comparable executive leadership positions in both the public and private sectors. The Board retains sole discretion and final authority to determine and approve the OHA Administrator's compensation package in accordance with its governing policies and all applicable laws.

Job Purpose

The Office of Hawaiian Affairs (OHA) works to improve the wellbeing of Native Hawaiians through advocacy, research, community engagement, land management and the funding of community programs.

The Administrator functions as the Chief Executive Officer ("CEO") of the Office of Hawaiian Affairs ("OHA") and is responsible for implementing and executing the will of the elected Board of Trustees (BOT). Reporting directly to the BOT, the Administrator & CEO provides executive oversight, strategic & operational leadership, and oversees organizational performance. The Administrator & CEO implements Board policy and advances OHA's constitutional and statutory responsibilities on behalf of Native Hawaiian beneficiaries.

The Administrator & CEO plays a central role in advancing this mission by ensuring that OHA’s people, programs, resources, and partnerships are aligned to achieve measurable results.  The Administrator & CEO maintains stewardship of the strategic planning process, ensuring alignment between Board direction, organizational priorities, operational execution, and performance outcomes.

As the principal executive of the OHA, this role serves as the conduit between the BOT, community, and administrative staff and is responsible for effective communication, leadership and direction.  Additionally, the Administrator & CEO works with other agencies, public and private, that also serve Hawaiians and Native Hawaiians consistent with OHA's mission of bettering the conditions of all Hawaiians.

Essential Responsibilities

Trustee Relations

The Administrator & CEO, selected by the Board of Trustees as the principal executive officer of the Office of Hawaiian Affairs, is responsible for the day-to-day management and administration of OHA under the Strategic Plan, policies, and actions adopted by the Board of Trustees.  In carrying out these duties, the Administrator shall develop, implement, and oversee organizational systems, operational procedures, and administrative processes, and shall make recommendations to the BOT regarding OHA's organizational structure.
Maintains a strong, transparent, and collaborative working relationship with the BOT, ensuring open communication, alignment on strategic priorities, and effective governance support.
Presents complex information to the Board in a clear, objective, and actionable manner, enabling informed governance, and strategic decision-making.   Identifies emerging trends, opportunities, and risks using data and research.

Collaboration/Leadership/Engagement

Responsible for strategic planning and execution.
Establishes clear vision and direction for the OHA staff and ensures that the OHA’s mission, core values, and principles are understood and put into practice.  Effectively mentors and empowers staff to create a healthy, positive, and culturally grounded environment that promotes accountability, transparency, and collaboration.
Fosters a positive work environment with strong values and integrity.  Motivates and encourages high performance and collaboration within all areas of the organization.
Develops and sustains a high-performing organization by identifying, developing, and preparing future leaders at all levels. Establishes succession strategies, leadership development programs, and knowledge transfer practices to ensure organizational continuity, preserve institutional knowledge, and maintain operational excellence.
Assesses the organization’s placement in the employment market to ensure the OHA continues to attract and retain talent of the highest quality to serve the mission.
Works cooperatively and collaboratively with others throughout the organization in alignment with the organization's objectives.

Operational Effectiveness

Monitors all critical organizational functions to ensure high performing operational excellence.
Ensures OHA is consistently aware of potential risks to the agency and its assets and is up to date with mitigation/avoidance strategies.

Fiscal & Asset Responsibility & Compliance

Responsible for fiscal and budget oversight and carries out the management of the OHA’s Native Hawaiian Trust Fund (NHTF) in accordance with the NHTF Investment Policy adopted by the BOT.
Responsible for procedures, guidelines, evaluation, contracts and grants that have been funded to promote services for OHA’s beneficiaries. 
Assumes overall accountability for the OHA’s successful operations, financial health, best practices, and overall legal compliance. 
Ensures OHA’s consistent compliance with local, state, and federal legal and regulatory requirements, , and best practices.

Community Relations & Advocacy

Is an effective liaison between the BOT, OHA, and Native Hawaiian Community.
Builds and maintains strong relationships with key stakeholders and the broader community, serving as one of OHA's three primary spokespersons under the direction of the BOT.
Communicates with beneficiaries and stakeholders in a consistent manner that results in mutual understanding, harmony, and action. 
Manages relationships to create optimal opportunities and moves the organization forward.
Serves as a legislative advocate under the direction of the BOT and is responsible for developing and monitoring the OHA’s legislative package.

Minimum Qualifications

A master's degree from an accredited college or university is required.  Degrees in business administration, public administration, public policy, finance, economics, law, organizational leadership, or a closely related field. An equivalent combination of education and experience may substitute for this degree requirement.
At least ten (10) years’ experience as a senior executive for a non-profit or for-profit organization/company, public administration, and/or executive leadership is required, of which the last five years must be at executive or leadership levels.
Experience leading strategic planning, organizational transformation, financial stewardship, and enterprise-wide change initiatives.
Experience leading similar sized, multidisciplinary organizations through organizational change while maintaining high levels of employee engagement and organizational effectiveness.
Demonstrated ability to develop collaborative partnerships with diverse stakeholders, including governmental agencies, community organizations, Native Hawaiian organizations, educational institutions, nonprofit organizations, and private-sector partners.

Excellent written, verbal, interpersonal, and public communication skills.

Desired Qualifications

The Board of Trustees is committed to recruiting the strongest executive talent available and will establish a competitive compensation package commensurate with the successful candidate's qualifications, experience, demonstrated leadership, and prevailing market conditions.

Pursuant to § 3.10.h of the OHA Executive Policy Manual, the Board of Trustees has the exclusive authority to establish the compensation of the OHA Administrator. In determining an appropriate compensation package, the Board may consider the 2025 State of Hawaiʻi Commission on Salaries Executive Compensation Schedule as one point of reference. The current Tier 1 executive salary range established by the Commission is $225,324 to $263,592 annually.
However, the Board is not limited to any particular salary schedule, benchmark, or compensation range in fulfilling its fiduciary responsibilities.

In establishing an appropriate compensation package, the Board may also consider the successful candidate's qualifications, executive experience, demonstrated leadership accomplishments, current market conditions, recruitment needs, and compensation for comparable executive leadership positions in both the public and private sectors. This position is listed on behalf of a partner company, who manages all applications and next steps. Our partner is looking for an Agile Program Director based in United States.

This leadership role is responsible for guiding large-scale Agile delivery initiatives and enabling high-performing teams through Lean-Agile practices.

The position serves as a strategic facilitator for Agile Release Train operations, improving collaboration, transparency, and delivery outcomes across multiple teams.

You will partner with product, engineering, business stakeholders, and Agile practitioners to drive alignment and continuous improvement.

The role combines coaching, program execution, risk management, and operational excellence within a regulated healthcare technology environment.

You will help establish effective Agile rhythms, optimize workflows, and promote a culture of innovation and accountability.

This remote opportunity is ideal for an experienced Agile leader who thrives in complex environments and enjoys empowering teams to deliver meaningful results.

Accountabilities

The Agile Program Director will serve as a servant leader and Agile coach, responsible for enabling effective program execution, improving delivery flow, and supporting teams in adopting scalable Agile practices. This role requires strong facilitation skills, strategic thinking, and the ability to influence stakeholders across the organization.

Facilitate Agile Release Train (ART) events, including PI Planning, ART Syncs, System Demos, and Inspect & Adapt sessions.
Prepare and coordinate PI Planning activities to ensure alignment around shared objectives, priorities, and delivery commitments.
Manage and continuously improve Program Kanban practices, applying flow metrics and WIP limits to optimize delivery performance.
Monitor ART predictability, delivery outcomes, risks, and dependencies while providing transparent reporting to stakeholders.
Support budget and delivery reporting through data-driven insights and performance tracking.
Facilitate risk management activities using ROAM practices and ensure risks are actively managed through resolution.
Partner with Product Management and Engineering teams to improve backlog readiness, prioritization, and execution alignment.
Coach Scrum Masters, Product Owners, business stakeholders, and leadership teams on Lean-Agile principles and servant leadership.
Manage, mentor, and develop Scrum Masters and Agile team coaches to strengthen team effectiveness.
Promote DevOps practices, continuous delivery capabilities, and built-in quality approaches.
Support compliance-focused delivery practices within regulated environments involving sensitive healthcare information.

Requirements

The ideal candidate is an experienced Agile delivery leader with a strong background in program-level facilitation, coaching, and enterprise Agile transformation. Success in this role requires strong communication skills, stakeholder management capabilities, and experience working with complex cross-functional teams.

6+ years of experience in Agile delivery, including at least 2 years in a program-level facilitation or coaching role such as Release Train Engineer or Senior Scrum Master.
Experience managing, mentoring, or coaching Scrum Masters or Agile team coaches.
Proven experience facilitating SAFe PI Planning and ART-level ceremonies.
Strong understanding of ART/Program Kanban, dependency management, risk management, and Agile flow metrics.
Experience using Agile ALM tools such as Azure DevOps, Jira, and virtual collaboration platforms.
Excellent communication, coaching, and interpersonal skills with the ability to influence stakeholders at all levels.
Strong results-oriented mindset with the ability to drive continuous improvement.
Experience working in healthcare IT environments and understanding of privacy or regulatory requirements preferred.
SAFe® Release Train Engineer (RTE) or SAFe® Program Consultant (SPC) certification preferred.
Knowledge of DevOps practices, CALMR principles, and Continuous Delivery Pipelines preferred.

Opportunity to lead impactful Agile transformation initiatives in a healthcare technology environment.
Collaborative culture focused on innovation, continuous improvement, and team empowerment.
